content:
sara: quick heads-up: found a repro where HF jinja chat_template -> Redwood converter drops the assistant marker when template ends with a trailing comment + jinja whitespace trim. reproducible locally.
kevin: ouch. paste minimal repro?
sara: minimal jinja (repro.j2):
```
{% macro pair(u,a) -%}
System: You are an assistant.
User: {{ u }}
Assistant: {{ a }}
{%- endmacro %}
{{ pair('hi','hello') }}  # trailing comment
```
kevin: and converted output?
sara: current naive conversion output (missing assistant sentinel / role boundary):
```
System: You are an assistant.
User: hi
hello
```
morgan: i.e. assistant label merged into body. the `-`/`-%}` trimming removed the newline our regex relies on to detect the role.
anita: did you check token ids pre/post conversion? that could cause downstream kv alignment issues when quantizing.
sara: yep. token diffs on a tiny sample: before conversion (we insert surrogate `<<assistant>>` marker): `[..., 50256, 1011, 2154, ...]` vs after: `[..., 1011, 2154, ...]` — sentinel (50256) gone, so offsets shift.
kevin: offset shift + quantization = recipe for visible quality regression. what quant runs did we try?
sara: ran eval harness 50 prompts: f32 baseline vs 8-bit. mean logprob delta f32->8bit = -0.18 without fix. after forcing explicit markers in converter patch, delta improved to -0.047. both runs on same dedicated infra.
morgan: patch idea?
sara: quick patch: ensure we always emit explicit role markers, even if body.strip() empty or trim swallowed newline. minimal change in conv module: after role mapping, if role=="Assistant" and marker not found in output, append `\n<<assistant>>\n`. also added converter warn log when template ends with inline comment.
kevin: temporary mitigation good. add unit test covering `-%}` + trailing comment combos. also log a converter:warn event.
anita: long-term we should stop splitting by regex and instead render using jinja AST so role nodes are explicit and whitespace control doesn't affect semantics.
morgan: agree. can we also check config.json artifacts? some HF models have null bos/eos ids. removing sentinel changes forced prefix decoding.
sara: good catch  i scanned two recently onboarded HF models: `bos_token_id` was null in their config.json. i added a conversion check that injects a safe synthetic BOS textual sentinel when bos_token_id is null and record the synthetic id mapping in metadata.
eval-bot: scheduled job `template-eval-repro` started (job-id repro-452)
kevin: add a small token-level roundtrip test to onboarding CI comparing token ids between HF-rendered and Redwood-converted templates. even a small mismatch should fail.
sara: done in PR branch. test harness prints token sequences and diffs. repro commands for local dev:
```
python -c "from conv import convert_chat_template; print(convert_chat_template(open('repro.j2').read()))"
python -c "from tokenizer import tok; print(tok.encode(open('converted.txt').read()))"
```
kevin: numbers when job finishes?
eval-bot: job `template-eval-repro` completed: mean logprob delta f32->8bit = -0.047 (n=50), p-value < 0.01. converter warns emitted for 3 templates in corpus.
morgan: please open PR, add unit tests + note in onboarding docs. also add a short-term hotfix release to nightly if CI green.
sara: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/conv/pull/342 — includes regression harness, testcases, and quant eval logs in PR description.
kevin: assigning to eng-ml for review and merge. @morgan please review.
morgan: will review EOD. if green we cut hotfix.
anita: plan summary: (1) short-term force markers + tests + hotfix, (2) mid-term rewrite converter to jinja AST emitter, (3) long-term onboarding CI fuzzing comparing token streams and automated quant regressions.
sara: final note: subtle interplay of jinja whitespace control and our regex-based splitting. tagging onboarding docs and creating a checklist for model owners about `bos_token_id` and trailing-comment patterns.
